language.howToChooseYourGradeIntro: Our curriculum Grades K to 6 corresponds with ages:
language.howToChooseYourGradeContent:
It’s very important children start at the right level, have fun in learning and work at their own pace. Please help the children selecting the level that is not too easy, but also not too difficult for them. There are two ways to do this.

  • You can either check the learning goals yourself to determine the correct level for your child(ren).
  • Or you can let the child take several lessons to determine his or her level. For example, if your child has the age of 6, please let him or her take one lesson in grade K, one lesson in grade 1, and one lesson in grade 2 to determine at which level he or she is.

dialog.text: Hello, I am Tim.

Hi, my name is Johny and I work on a Crab Boat. I go out to sea for months together to catch crab. I only come back to shore when the boat is full! I spend so much time with crabs that I´ve come to know them quite well.
Did you know that humans and crabs have a lot in common? For example, both humans and crabs move, they both respire and they both reproduce.
All these things are called life processes. There are 7 life processes that all living beings undergo. Are you ready to learn more about these? Let's go!
Can you help Johny name the 7 life processes?

We all need energy to survive. We humans do, and crabs do too. We get this energy from two things: eating and breathing. Oxygen in the air is combined with sugar in our food to make energy.
This is called respiration. Do you know which organs in our bodies help with respiration, to make sure we always have enough energy?

All humans and animals need to eat to live. They take in food into their mouths and chew it with their teeth, which breaks the food down so it can be taken into the stomach. Can you help me answer whether these statements about nutrition are true or false?

helperSimple.text: All living things need food and water to survive. We call this life process 'nutrition'. Can you help Johny with his questions on nutrition? Read the statement he has written down and tell him if it's true or false.

Another life process is excretion. You know how all animals eat and drink? Well, all the things we don't need must also go out.
We call these things we don't need waste and the process of getting them out is called excretion. A lot of organs play a role in this. Can you select the correct organ to complete the sentence?
